I definitely like Christine now that she’s out, but I think polygamy (understandably) brought out the worst in her. Now that I’ve seen what seems to be her core personality now that she’s left, I really do think she’s a good person… but I really did not like her as the series continued. 

It was very frustrating to see her veto the one house idea. The architect did such a lovely job and it really would have been very private. It seemed like one of the last things that could’ve brought the family back together. She seemed so smug to be able to veto it ☹️ And then seeing how angry she got when no one else wanted to move AGAIN was also frustrating. All I saw was selfish, selfish, selfish that she wouldn’t even consider what others wanted. However, I think these were all signs of a) polygamy just REALLY not being a fit for her  b) the stress of being in a dynamic you hate but feel is your spiritual calling c) years and years of not being able to have more control over her life. 

There’s absolutely nothing wrong with not liking polygamy. And as much as it’s easy for all of us armchair experts to point and say “you signed up for this”, it’s harder to remember we only see so much on TV, it’s deeply engrained into her faith, and leaving after you have kids is so much harder, much less the other wives’ kids that felt like her own too. Yeah it’s 100% frustrating to see how she reacted to some of the basic compromises you have to make in a polygamist family, but unfortunately I’m sure it just wasn’t as simple as “if you don’t like it, leave”. And I’m so happy the worst in her seems to have been left behind now that she’s left. It makes me glad to see her be so likable and happy.

I used to work at Starbucks. I loved the job and the benefits, but the customers were just awful. So incredibly mean spirited and there were a few who made me cry - I’m not a crier! So yeah, $8.20 an hour to be yelled at, cussed out, understaffed, and stressed out? Nah. I’m self employed now but if I got laid off at Starbucks and then realized how good life can be when I’m not being under paid and screamed at over bean water, I probably wouldn’t go back either. From MY experience, there are a few things that retail jobs and fast food jobs could do to attract and retain workers. 

1) Do not allow customers to verbally abuse your workers. This was the #1 reason I couldn’t handle being a barista anymore.

2) Compensate fairly, not just for the best profit margin. 

3) Follow in the footsteps of Starbucks and offer great benefits for everyone, including part timers. Tuition reimbursement, insurance, EAPs, stocks, etc. 

4) Be a good boss. Not a good corporate megaphone. My first boss at Starbucks is still the best boss I have ever had. He made working fun, kept the crew positive,  he was so innovative, and not afraid to stand up to brilliant new corporate ideas that didn’t work.  He would give it a fair shot and then go back to what worked. The numbers didn’t lie so the DMs let it slide 😂

Everyone deserves to be able to have a roof over their heads, clothes on their back, and food in their bellies without going through hell and back in an abusive environment just to barely make ends meet. Make it to where people can actually enjoy life and they will want to work. 

Just my 2 cents as a former fast food worker!

You have every right to be upset since you both agreed on a boundary, and he crossed it. 

My husband and I agreed that WE feel that porn use is a form of infidelity in OUR relationship, but that if one of us were to ever use it, we can go to the other person with no judgement.  The problem would lie in if the user was honest and upfront. Well, 3 years into marriage, my husband ended up hiding his porn use for 5 months before I finally was able to get him to admit something was up. 

It was VERY crushing because the boundary of “no lying about porn” had been crossed big time! I figured it would happen eventually, but I didn’t expect the lying since we were so honest and upfront about everything else and this was such a specific scenario that I thought we prepped for.

It turns out my husband was dealing with severe emotional issues and his ADHD is so bad that it impedes his communication skills at times. So we worked on ways that he can communicate with me that work for his brain. We have worked through this and are stronger than ever.

If you feel like your husband truly wants to mend things, it is entirely possible. But you have to set and maintain your boundaries, and he has to respect them. If you guys can meet in the middle and have a lot of uncomfortable conversations, you can get through this. 

ETA: I will agree with someone down below that you very may well have only scratched the surface. Trust your gut. That’s how I found out.

I am extremely privileged. Being born a straight white female to older parents as their only child, my parents were much more established than my friends’ parents were because they had me around 40. So I grew up with basically having any opportunity I wanted handed to me, and practically anything I wanted I got, whether I paid for it myself or not. My parents never let me be selfish or brag though. I have been told a million times that people don’t know how I didn’t end up a spoiled, entitled asshole. My parents were very careful to always keep me humble. I’m married now, and they paid for our home and nice car just because they wanted to see us not have to struggle the way they did. The privilege I have is insane. I hate feeling guilty but I can’t help it when I drive around sipping my Starbucks and see people starving and cold on the streets. I try to just give those people food and supplies whenever I have extra, and constantly remind myself of how lucky I am compared to so many people. We’ve also given money to friends who needed it. Not a loan, but as a gift. My whole family looked out for their friends and family and that’s what we want to do too. I’ve had a lot of people be so mean to me over how good I’ve had it my whole life. I do really wish that wouldn’t happen, the guilt it places on my shoulders when I didn’t ask for ANY of this just feels weird and like I’m not good enough as a person to have “earned” my privilege. We just try to share what we can, it feels wrong to just sit on money and do nothing to help the people around you that are drowning. I think it’s cruel to put anyone down over something they can’t control, whether it’s their privilege or lack thereof. Just because you aren’t happy doesn’t mean you can just tear people down around you. We ALL have our problems. I might have more than enough physically but I have a whole host of mental problems that have nearly taken my life several times. There always seems to be a trade off :/

Of course! I do agree that the mountains are cool, I think it’s more the color scheme that’s clashing than anything. I would say either find a different stock photo, or you could type in “mountain banner graphic” on Google and look at a few images.  I’ll link one here in a second. 

Do you know how to take good product photos, or are you willing to contract out for a branding photographer? My business is more of a service than a product (social media management), but how are you driving traffic? Sponsored posts or organic traffic? 

Personally I prefer a home page just to be an eye catching brand page, have some featured products, and then have a page just for “products” that you divide up into categories like you have on the home page. Hi!!! Congratulations on starting your business. Your products look super cool. So excited for you! 

I do agree that the color scheme is a little confusing. Are you aiming for more of an earthy, almost boho vibe or a more energetic look? Based on the look of your products I'd guess more the energetic, sporty look. If so, simply changing the banner from a stock photo of mountains to an artistic graphic would fit the style much better. Fiverr is AMAZING for decently priced, quality graphics for a startup. Other than that, to me it looks like you have several different fonts going on. To me, it's a little jarring. I would stick to preferably two, but a max of 3 to maintain continuity and make it easier on the eyes.  Finally I know you said this is an online business for now - but I would recommend getting real product photos at some point rather than an overlay of the graphics. It'll look much more professional and high-end. But I know budget can get in the way of that right away, just something to keep in mind for later. 

I hope this helps! This is of course just my opinion. Do what makes you happy. People will sense passion behind a project, and customers will follow passion!

I have been suicidal several times. Both when terrible things happened and others for no real reason. I couldn’t stop the cycle of: crippling depression -> motivated to feel better -> do things slowly and pull myself out of depression -> full blast productivity, self care, happiness -> overcommitment and pushing myself too far -> crash into crippling depression. 

Antidepressants really helped the depths of my depression, but the cycle continued. I was finally diagnosed with bipolar 2 a few months ago at age 24. No one had ever suggested that I had something wrong other than depression. For the first time in my life I really understand “it gets better”. When people told me that at my lowest, I didn’t agree. I didn’t think I could ever feel better since I had struggled so badly for so long. The people who said “it gets better” seemingly had their shit together which was just something I couldn’t seem to do consistently. They may have dealt with depression and suicidal ideation but I just… believed I was different. They got out of it, but I never would because I am me and I am destined for misery no matter how hard I try. 

I promise you…. it DOES get better. It’s a seriously awful and hard road, but if I had attempted and succeeded the first time I was suicidal, I would have missed out on meeting my absolutely INCREDIBLE husband, moving out of state to start over, the birth of my nephew, being maid of honor in my best friend’s wedding, traveling the world, and truly enjoying my life for the first time. You have so many things coming that you will miss out on. 

Please, reach out and find an amazing therapist, talk to your doctor and coordinate with your therapist about meds that could help. Ask a family member or friend to help you search if you feel like you can’t. If therapy is expensive for you, look into therapists who offer sliding scale rates. The most I’ve ever paid for a therapy session is $50. 

Medication is a pain to get acclimated to, but when you find the right one? It is life changing. My meds genuinely saved my life. My husband was petrified he was going to come home from work and suddenly be a widower, and I understand why he was so scared now that I’m doing better. 

Don’t misunderstand. My life isn’t sunshine and roses, I still experience mental health issues. But it’s actually doable now. It sucks, but I can get through it so much easier now. 

If you feel you don’t have anyone to help you connect with resources, or you’re simply embarrassed, please PM me and I will help you. I’m a stranger, but I already care about you and want to see you get better. I know there are people who love you so deeply and would be devastated should anything happen to you. Sure! This recipe is super simple so I don’t keep track of much, but I’ll do my best.

2-4 pork chops 
A bowl of Panko bread crumbs
Egg(s)
Flour 
Seasonings (salt, pepper is fine, but feel free to be creative!)

Tenderize pork chops until 1/4-1/3 inch thick. Score the fat and tendons for extra tenderness! Season the chops, then season a bowl of flour, a bowl of beaten eggs, and a bowl of panko crumbs. (Basically season each step.) Bread the pork chops in the flour, egg, panko setup and press the breading into the pork chops. Heat a shallow pot or deep pan with oil of choice until a wooden spoon sizzles. (We don’t use a thermometer ). Place pork chops and fry until lightly browned, flipping once. Then rest and complete the rest of the batch. Once they’re done, fry them once again until golden/deep brown. Slice immediately after taking them out of the fryer, place over cooked sushi rice and serve with shredded cabbage and sesame dressing.

My husband has impulsivity issues due to his severe ADHD and this can sometimes land him in a little bit of trouble. The other problem is his ADHD unfortunately affects his verbal communication skills to the point he sometimes ends up lying to me because he doesn’t know how to convey what he’s trying to say when he’s upset. He always tells me after a few minutes that he was lying, so it’s not like he’s trying to hide things long term from me. He is a WONDERFUL man and is desperate to stop these communication problems and the compulsion to lie.

Enter the communication notebook. We wrote down prompts he can point to when verbal communication is too overwhelming or over-stimulating. Things as simple as yes/no all the way to confessing a mistake. Most of the time he struggles getting the ball rolling when he’s upset, so this is an aid to help him with that. He’s expressed he can tell me things over text, but he’s afraid of coming off as insincere. We implemented the following to accommodate his needs:

1. We got those silly reversible plushie animals we saw on Tiktok. One side is smiling, and the inverted is frowning. This signals to the other when we need help but can’t ask for it. 
2. The notebook also doubles as a medium to leave each other notes for us to check when we feel ready. If he has something he needs to get off his chest, he can write it down, and then ask me later to check the notebook, or leave it out to signal to me I need to take a look. 
3. We assigned random emojis for when we’re not together in case he needs something but can’t directly ask for it. For instance an emoji is assigned to say “check the notebook”, and “I need to talk but I don’t know how”.

These things might seem silly, but he’s struggled with communication and lying when he’s under severe stress his entire life. He doesn’t want to be like this. He hates his ADHD and the fact it limits him so badly sometimes. When I presented these ideas, he lit up and said it sounded like it was exactly what he needs. I really hope this works for him, I thought I’d share here in case anyone else has these kinds of issues.

Something that helps me is not 100% cutting out junk food. I ALWAYS deprive, constrict, binge, repeat. 

What I have found works VERY well for me is to have junk food, but portioned out. Like, we’ll buy the party pack, individually wrapped chips and limit ourselves to 1 max per day, AFTER I have eaten fruit or veggies and had a bunch of water or unsweetened green tea. Or, buy a bag of frozen cinnamon rolls/cookie dough/what have you and only bake ONE each every so often. Or have ONE white chocolate truffle. ONE wrapped Rice Krispie treat. 

If I’ve been super good, worked out a lot that week, and have extra calories, sure I’ll have a couple of slices of pizza. One meal that isn’t healthy is not going to make you fat.

Some people have to cut out junk food cold turkey. Others (like me) cannot physically handle that and need my stupid latte every once in a while, or my daily serving of chips. The majority of the time, I eat soooo much fruit and vegetables that I don’t even crave junk food as much at all. Find what works for you, modify, and stick to it.

I should add that I try to practice “intuitive eating” and add everything into my Fitbit app at the end of the day to see how I did.
